newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOCCER - All Whites end tour with a draw.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - All Whites end tour with a draw.

text.p: BEIRUT, Lebanon, Oct 9 - A 78th minute goal by Darren McClennan rescued a 10-man New Zealand team from a losing end to their Middle East soccer tour, instead earning a 1-1 draw with Lebanon after they trailed 1-0 at halftime, NZPA reported on Thursday (NZT).
The All Whites leave the Middle East with two wins, two losses and a draw, but it took a second half effort masterminded by Michael McGarry to conjure up a result.
It was a game the Kiwis could have won -- after fluffing two excellent first half chances -- but after weathering a hectic late Lebanese onslaught, they left the Bourj Hammoud Stadium happy.

It was another frustrating day for the side with Andy Rennie becoming the second New Zealander in two games to be sent off, when he received a second yellow card for a tackle 15 minutes into the half.
That followed Wynton Rufer's dismissal in the last game against Qatar.
The loss of Rennie forced McGarry to resume his centre midfield role of previous games, and New Zealand looked a much more positive outfit for it.

McClennan had missed a golden opportunity to take the lead in the first half, shooting wide one-on-one with the keeper but all was forgotten when he collected a ball from McGarry via Waitakere team-mate Mark Elrick.

On level terms the New Zealanders played their best soccer of the game and Elrick almost snatched a victory with four minutes to play with a 35 metre shot which hit the crossbar. The goal was a fitting reward for McClennan, who at times has had a tough time from defenders on this tour.
"It's nice to get something at the end of the tour," he said.
"You're prepared for physical games all the time but it's tough when you don't get much protection from the referee.
"From that comes frustration and perhaps you should be able to deal with it but when its going on game in, game out you can start to lose the plot."
The Lebanese too had some golden opportunities to put the game beyond doubt, but poor finishing, combined with more heroics from Jason Batty in goal kept New Zealand in touch.
The first half began in dramatic fashion as Lebanon's Tru Khyeyan found a gap in the defence in the second minute and seemed sure to score, from five metres.
Batty, aggressive as usual, proved enough of a distraction, however, and the shot went wide.
The two best chances fell to New Zealand, however.
In the 10th minute a ball from Chris Jackson found McCLennan on his own at the edge of the box -- in a position he would bury the ball from nine times out of 10.
Incredibly he hit it wide, while 10 minutes later Mark Elrick was put into similar space by Michael McGarry only to take too much time on the ball as the defence rushed home.
Four minutes later Wartan Gazarian was through one-on-one with Batty and his time there was no mistake.
Batty forced another mis-shot from Jamal Taha on the half-hour while in the 37th minute Elrick curled in a corner forcing a good save from the Lebanese keeper.
Too many mistakes from the New Zealanders prevented real pressure being applied to what looked a fragile Lebanon defence, however.
Balls were kicked out and passes went astray far too often. Coach Keith Pritchett went away from the match happy.
"I wasn't pleased with the first half -- again we sat back too much, though we created some good chances," he said.
"The second half was a lot better and I could defend Andy Rennie's second yellow card. Down to 10 men I think we played very well and Michael McGarry was superb," he said.
The Middle East experience is definitely one Pritchett would repeat.
"I'd certainly come here again, and after getting two wins and a draw on this trip I think the whole Middle East will be looking at us as possible opponents," he said.
"These countries are playing 15 to 20 internationals a year so there is an opportunity for games virtually all year round."
The starting lineup was: Jason Batty, Chris Zoricich, Rodger Gray, Andy Rennie, Jason New, Graham Marshall, Michael McGarry, Chris Jackson, Simon Elliott, Darren McClennan, Mark Elrick.
Substitutes: Danny Hay for Rodger Gray, (75 minutes), Nik Viljoen for McClennan (81 minutes).
